newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela lower house OKs refinancing debt to cenbank. [CORRECTED 23:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela lower house OKs refinancing debt to cenbank. [CORRECTED 23:25 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to say the lower house of Congress approved the refinancing, not a committee.)
Venezuela's lower house of Congress approved Thursday in second reading a bill that would refinance the government's $3.89 billion debt to the Central Bank, legislators said.
The law, "which will allow the Bank's accounts to return to equilibrium, now goes to the Senate for final approval," said Congressman Rodrigo Cabezas from opposition union-based party Radical Cause.
The proposed law allows the Central Bank to use Treasury bills, backed by the debt, to conduct monetary operations alongside the currently used Central Bank-backed TEMs.

Imbalances between the Central Bank's low-yielding assets -- including government debt -- and its costly liabilities -- principally TEMs -- brought the Bank a 45 billion bolivar ($96 million) loss over the first half of 1996.
The Central Bank assumed the debt in 1990 to guarantee sovereign debt, including Venezuela's Brady bonds.
